chunks: As for your saying: Why did you set a time limit between yourself and them regarding the Arbitration?

I did so only so that the ignorant may become clear (about the truth), and the knowledgeable may hold firm, and perhaps Allah will rectify the affairs of this community during this truce, and they will not be seized by their throats, so that they hasten to recognize the truth and submit to the first deviation.

Indeed, the best of people before Allah is he who loves acting according to the truth more—even if it diminishes and grieges him—than acting according to falsehood, even if it brings him benefit and increase.

key_terms.التَّحْكِيمِ: Arbitration (referring to the judgment of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and Amr ibn al-Aas)

ai.seo_question: What was the wisdom behind Imam Ali's delay in the Arbitration with the Kharijites?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) justifies the temporary truce of Siffin as a strategic pause to distinguish the sincere from the ignorant, aiming to prevent hasty submission to error while allowing for potential divine rectification of the Ummah. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'tahkim' (arbitration) not as a concession of weakness, but as a calculated measure to preserve the integrity of truth over expedient falsehood. The concluding principle underscores that true piety is measured by adherence to truth even when it entails personal loss, rather than seeking worldly benefit through compromise.
